stem.en: Kabir asks how the brain "knows how hot the diya was, if every nerve wave is the same size". What carries the strength of a stimulus?

text.en: How many waves per second, and how many nerves fire. A hotter diya makes the fingertip's nerves fire far more often, and recruits more of them. Loudness is in the rate, not the size.

feedback.en: Every spike is the same height. The sim showed it.
Speed is set by the cable, from tomorrow, not the stimulus.
The brain reads rates and which nerves are firing. That is enough to tell warm from scalding.

explanation.en: All-or-none spikes carry nothing in their size. They carry it in their timing and their number.
